title.zh: 卷443 列傳二百三十 孙家鼐 张百熙 唐景崇 於式枚 沈家本
title.en: Volume 443 Biographies 230: Sun Jianai, Zhang Baixi, Tang Jingchong, Yu Shimei, Shen Jiaben
title.raw: 卷443 列傳二百三十 孙家鼐 张百熙 唐景崇 於式枚 沈家本

sentences.zh: 孫家鼐，字燮臣，安徽壽州人。

translations.literal: Sun Jianai, style name Xiecheng, was a man of Shouzhou, Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Jianai, whose style was Xiecheng, came from Shouzhou in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年一甲一名進士，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng he was a jinshi of the first class, first rank, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Xianfeng reign he took first place in the top tier of the jinshi examinations and was appointed a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 歷侍讀，入直上書房。

translations.literal: He successively served as reader-in-waiting and entered service in the Imperial Study.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the post of reader-in-waiting and entered the Imperial Study.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，命在毓慶宮行走，與尚書翁同龢授上讀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he was ordered to serve as attendant at the Yuying Palace, and together with Minister Weng Tonghe instructed the emperor in reading.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Guangxu reign he was assigned to attend at the Yuying Palace, where he and Minister Weng Tonghe served as the emperor's reading tutors.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士，擢工部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and was elevated to vice minister of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat and then elevated to vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 江西學政陳寶琛疏請以先儒黃宗羲、顧炎武從祀文廟，議者多以爲未可，家鼐與潘祖蔭、翁同龢、孫詒經等再請，始議准。

translations.literal: Chen Baochen, educational commissioner of Jiangxi, memorialized requesting that the early Ruists Huang Zongxi and Gu Yanwu be granted posthumous worship in the Confucian temple. Most who deliberated held it inadvisable. Jianai, together with Pan Zuyin, Weng Tonghe, Sun Yizhen, and others petitioned again, and only then was approval granted in discussion.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Baochen, the Jiangxi educational commissioner, memorialized that the early masters Huang Zongxi and Gu Yanwu be admitted to worship in the Confucian temple, most deliberators judged the proposal premature. Jianai joined Pan Zuyin, Weng Tonghe, Sun Yizhen, and others in petitioning again, and only then did the court approve the measure.

sentences.zh: 十六年，授都察院左都御史、工部尚書，兼順天府尹。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed left censor-in-chief of the Censorate and minister of the Ministry of Works, and concurrently served as prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In his sixteenth year of service he was made left censor-in-chief of the Censorate and minister of works, while also holding the post of Shuntian prefect.

sentences.zh: 二十年，中日事起，朝議主戰，家鼐力言釁不可啓。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year trouble arose between China and Japan. Court opinion favored war, but Jianai strongly argued that hostilities must not be provoked.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year the Sino-Japanese crisis erupted. The court leaned toward war, but Jianai insisted that the quarrel must not be opened.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以吏部尚書協辦大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, as minister of the Ministry of Personnel he was appointed associate grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed associate grand secretary while serving as minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 命爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve as superintendent of studies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed superintendent of studies.

sentences.zh: 時方議變法，廢科舉，興學校，設報編書，皆特交核覆，家鼐一裁以正。

translations.literal: At the time reform was under discussion: abolishing the civil-service examinations, establishing schools, founding newspapers, and compiling books—all were specially referred to him for review and reply, and Jianai settled each matter on proper grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Reform was then in the air—abolishing the examinations, founding schools, launching newspapers, commissioning new books—and each proposal was sent to him for final review. Jianai judged every one on its merits and set policy straight.

sentences.zh: 嘗疏謂：「國家廣集卿士以資議政，聽言固不厭求詳，然執兩用中，精擇審處，尤賴聖知。

translations.literal: He once memorialized, saying: "The state broadly gathers high officials to supply deliberation on government. In hearing words one certainly does not tire of seeking detail, yet in holding to the mean between two sides, in finely choosing and carefully disposing, one relies especially on sagely understanding."
translations.idiomatic: He once wrote in a memorial: "The state gathers its senior ministers so that policy may be debated in full. It is right to welcome detailed counsel, yet to hold the middle course, to choose wisely and act with care, depends above all on the sovereign's discernment."

sentences.zh: 」其所建議，類能持大體。

translations.literal: His proposals were generally able to uphold the larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: The proposals he advanced generally upheld the larger principles of governance.

sentences.zh: 及議廢立，家鼐獨持不可。

translations.literal: When the question of deposing and enthroning was discussed, Jianai alone held that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated deposing the emperor and installing another, Jianai alone maintained that the move was impermissible.

sentences.zh: 旋以病乞罷。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he pleaded illness and requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，乘輿西狩，召赴行在，起禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, when the imperial carriage went west on a hunting tour, he was summoned to the temporary court and reappointed minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, when the court fled west, he was summoned to the temporary capital and reinstated as minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 還京，拜體仁閣大學士。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital he was appointed grand secretary of the Tiren Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After the return to Beijing he was made grand secretary of the Tiren Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 歷轉東閣、文淵閣，晉武英殿。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession through the Eastern Pavilion and Wenyuan Pavilion, and was promoted to the Hall of Martial Eminence.
translations.idiomatic: He moved in turn through the Eastern and Wenyuan pavilions before advancing to the Hall of Martial Eminence.

sentences.zh: 充學務大臣，裁度規章，折衷中外，嚴定宗旨，一以敦行實學爲主，學風爲之一靖。

translations.literal: He served as minister of educational affairs, measured and set regulations, balanced Chinese and foreign elements, strictly fixed the guiding purpose, and took practical learning in earnest conduct as the sole standard, so that academic custom was calmed thereby.
translations.idiomatic: As minister of educational affairs he framed regulations, balanced Chinese and Western approaches, and fixed a clear purpose: practical learning pursued in earnest conduct. Under his direction academic life grew noticeably more orderly.

sentences.zh: 議改官制，命與慶親王奕劻、軍機大臣瞿鴻禨總司核定。

translations.literal: When reform of the official system was discussed, he was ordered together with Prince Qing Yikuang and Grand Councilor Qu Hongji to take overall charge of verification and approval.
translations.idiomatic: When official reform was debated, he was ordered to work with Prince Qing Yikuang and Grand Councilor Qu Hongji in supervising the final review.

sentences.zh: 御史趙啓霖劾奕劻及其子貝子載振受賄納優，命醇親王載灃與家鼐往按，啓霖坐汚衊親貴褫職，而載振尋亦乞罷兼官。

translations.literal: Censor Zhao Qilin impeached Yikuang and his son, the beile Zaizhen, for taking bribes and receiving actresses. The Prince Chun Zaifeng and Jianai were ordered to go investigate. Qilin was punished for slandering the imperial kin and was stripped of office, while Zaizhen soon also begged to resign his concurrent posts.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Zhao Qilin accused Yikuang and his son, the beile Zaizhen, of taking bribes and keeping actresses. Prince Chun Zaifeng and Jianai were sent to investigate. Qilin was dismissed for defaming the imperial kin, and Zaizhen soon resigned his concurrent offices as well.

sentences.zh: 資政院立，命貝子溥倫及家鼐爲總裁，一持正議不阿。

translations.literal: When the Political Consultative Council was established, the beile Pulun and Jianai were appointed presidents. He consistently upheld upright views and did not curry favor.
translations.idiomatic: When the Political Consultative Council was created, the beile Pulun and Jianai were named its presidents. Jianai held to principled positions and would not trim his views to please.

sentences.zh: 時詔諸臣輪班進講，家鼐撰尚書四子書講義以進。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered officials to lecture in rotation. Jianai composed expositions on the Book of Documents and the Four Books and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: The throne then ordered ministers to lecture in rotation; Jianai prepared commentaries on the Book of Documents and the Four Books and submitted them.

sentences.zh: 三十四年二月，以鄉舉重逢，賞太子太傅。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year, because he had again attained the provincial examination reunion, he was rewarded with the post of grand tutor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirty-fourth year he was honored as grand tutor of the heir apparent for having again reached the provincial-examination reunion milestone.

sentences.zh: 歷蒙賜「壽」，頒賞御書及諸珍品，賜紫韁，紫禁城內坐二人暖輪，恩遇優渥。

translations.literal: He repeatedly received the gift of the character "longevity," was granted imperial calligraphy and various precious objects, was given a purple bridle, and was allowed a two-seater heated carriage within the Forbidden City. His favor was exceptionally generous.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly granted the imperial character for longevity, imperial calligraphy, and other precious gifts; he received a purple bridle and permission to ride a two-seater heated carriage inside the Forbidden City. The court's favor toward him was exceptionally generous.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，再疏乞病，溫詔慰留。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he again memorialized pleading illness. A warm edict urged him to remain.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuantong reign he again asked to retire for illness, but a gracious edict urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年八十有二，贈太傅，諡文正。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died, at the age of eighty-two. He was posthumously granted the title of grand tutor and was given the posthumous name Wenzheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at eighty-two. The court posthumously honored him as grand tutor and gave him the posthumous name Wenzheng.

sentences.zh: 家鼐簡約斂退，生平無疾言遽色。

translations.literal: Jianai was simple and restrained in withdrawal. Throughout his life he had no harsh words or sudden changes of countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Jianai lived simply and kept himself in the background; he was never known for sharp words or a sudden change of expression.

sentences.zh: 雖貴，與諸生鈞禮。

translations.literal: Although eminent, he treated students with equal courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he rose high, he treated students as equals in courtesy.

sentences.zh: 閉門齋居，雜賓遠跡，推避權勢若怯。

translations.literal: He shut his door and lived in abstinent seclusion. Mixed guests kept their distance. He shrank from power as if from timidity.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his doors closed and lived quietly at home; casual visitors stayed away, and he avoided the powerful as if he were timid by nature.

sentences.zh: 嘗督湖北學政，典山西試，再典順天試，總裁會試，屢充閱卷大臣，獨無所私。

translations.literal: He once supervised educational affairs in Hubei, presided over the Shanxi examination, twice presided over the Shuntian examination, directed the metropolitan examination, and repeatedly served as chief examiner—yet he showed favoritism to none.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as Hubei educational commissioner, presided over the Shanxi provincial examination, twice directed the Shuntian examination, headed the metropolitan examination, and repeatedly served as chief examiner, yet he never showed favoritism.

sentences.zh: 嘗拔一卷廁二甲，同列意不可，即屏退之，其讓不喜競類此。

translations.literal: He once placed one examination paper in the second class of the second rank. His colleagues disapproved, and he immediately set it aside. His yielding and dislike of rivalry were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Once he placed a candidate's paper in the second class of the second rank; when his colleagues objected, he withdrew it at once. His willingness to yield and his dislike of rivalry were typical of him.

sentences.zh: 器量尤廣，庚子，外人請懲禍首戮大臣，編修劉廷琛謂失國體，責宰輔不能爭，家鼐揖而引過。

translations.literal: His capacity was especially broad. In the gengzi year foreigners demanded that the chief culprits among the ministers be punished and executed. Compiler Liu Tingchen said this would damage the dignity of the state and blamed the chief ministers for failing to remonstrate. Jianai bowed and took the blame upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: His forbearance was especially notable. In 1900, when foreigners demanded that leading ministers be punished and executed, compiler Liu Tingchen protested that this would humiliate the state and blamed the chief ministers for failing to stand their ground. Jianai bowed and accepted the fault himself.

sentences.zh: 其後詔舉御史。

translations.literal: Afterward an edict ordered the recommendation of censors.
translations.idiomatic: Later an edict called for nominations to the censorate.

sentences.zh: 家鼐獨保廷琛，謂曩以大義見責，知忠鯁必不負國，世皆稱之。

translations.literal: Jianai alone recommended Tingchen, saying that because he had earlier been reproached on grounds of great principle, one knew that his loyal bluntness would surely not fail the state. The world all praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Jianai alone recommended Tingchen, saying that a man who had once been rebuked for upholding the larger principle would surely prove loyal and blunt in the state's service. All who heard of it praised his judgment.

sentences.zh: 張百熙，字埜秋，長沙人。

translations.literal: Zhang Baixi, style name Yeqiu, was a man of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baixi, whose style was Yeqiu, came from Changsha.

sentences.zh: 同治十三年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tongzhi he became a jinshi and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of the Tongzhi reign he passed the jinshi examinations and was appointed a Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: 督山東學政，典試四川。

translations.literal: He supervised educational affairs in Shandong and presided over the examination in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Shandong educational commissioner and presided over the Sichuan provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 命直南書房，再遷侍讀。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve in the Southern Study and was promoted again to reader-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to the Southern Study and was later promoted to reader-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年，朝鮮釁起，朝議多主戰。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu trouble arose in Korea. Court opinion mostly favored war.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of the Guangxu reign conflict broke out in Korea, and most at court favored war.

sentences.zh: 百熙疏劾李鴻章陽作戰備，陰實主和，左寶貴、聶士成皆勇敢善戰之將，以餉械不繼，遂致敗績，咎在鴻章；

translations.literal: Baixi memorialized impeaching Li Hongzhang for outwardly making war preparations while inwardly actually favoring peace. Zuo Baogui and Nie Shicheng were both brave generals skilled in battle, but because pay and arms were not supplied in succession, defeat followed; the blame lay with Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Baixi memorialized against Li Hongzhang, charging that he made a show of preparing for war while secretly favoring peace. Generals Zuo Baogui and Nie Shicheng were both brave and capable fighters, yet because pay and arms failed to reach them in time, defeat followed—and the fault, Baixi argued, lay with Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 又劾禮親王世鐸筦樞務，招權納賄，戰事起，一倚鴻章，貽誤兵機：皆不報。

translations.literal: He also impeached Prince Li Shiduo for managing pivotal affairs, monopolizing power and taking bribes; when war arose he relied entirely on Hongzhang and thereby harmed military timing: none of these were answered.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached Prince Li Shiduo for monopolizing power at the Grand Council, taking bribes, and leaving the war entirely in Hongzhang's hands, thereby bungling military timing. None of his charges received a response.

sentences.zh: 時值太后萬壽，承辦典禮者猶競尚華飾，百熙奏罷之。

translations.literal: It happened to be the empress dowager's birthday celebration. Those in charge of the ceremonial still vied in extravagant ornament. Baixi memorialized to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's birthday fell at the same time, and those arranging the ceremonies still competed in lavish display. Baixi memorialized to have the extravagance stopped.

sentences.zh: 復偕侍講學士陸寶忠等合彈樞臣朋比誤國十大罪。

translations.literal: He again joined exposition lecturer Lu Baozhong and others in jointly impeaching the grand councilors for ten great crimes of faction and harming the state.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined exposition lecturer Lu Baozhong and others in a joint impeachment of the grand councilors on ten counts of factional collusion and damage to the state.

sentences.zh: 未幾，孫毓汶引疾歸，恭親王奕訢復入軍機，而百熙亦出督廣東學政。

translations.literal: Before long Sun Yuwen pleaded illness and returned home. Prince Gong Yixin re-entered the Grand Council, and Baixi also went out to supervise educational affairs in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Sun Yuwen retired on grounds of illness, Prince Gong Yixin returned to the Grand Council, and Baixi was sent out as Guangdong educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted step by step to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，坐濫舉康有爲，革職留任。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was punished for indiscriminately recommending Kang Youwei and was stripped of office while retained in his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was punished for improperly recommending Kang Youwei: his office was removed, but he was kept on in his duties.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授禮部侍郎，擢左都御史，充頭等專使大臣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed vice minister of the Ministry of Rites, was promoted to left censor-in-chief, and served as a first-rank special envoy minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he was made vice minister of rites, promoted to left censor-in-chief, and appointed a first-rank special envoy.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂定，下詔求言，百熙抗疏陳大計，請改官制，理財政，變科舉，建學堂，設報館。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil was settled, an edict sought opinions. Baixi submitted a forthright memorial setting forth the great plan, requesting reform of the official system, regulation of finances, transformation of the examinations, establishment of schools, and founding of newspapers.
translations.idiomatic: After the Boxer uprising was suppressed, the throne called for counsel. Baixi submitted a bold memorial outlining a comprehensive program: reform the bureaucracy, put finances in order, transform the examinations, build schools, and establish newspapers.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷工部尚書，調刑部，充管學大臣。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to minister of the Ministry of Works, was moved to the Ministry of Punishments, and served as superintendent of studies.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was made minister of works, transferred to the Ministry of Punishments, and appointed superintendent of studies.

sentences.zh: 京師之有大學堂也，始於中日戰後。

translations.literal: The existence of a university hall in the capital began after the Sino-Japanese war.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing's Imperial University dated from the period after the Sino-Japanese War.

sentences.zh: 侍郎李端棻奏請立學，中旨報可，而樞府厭言新政，請緩行。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Li Duanfen memorialized requesting the establishment of the school. An imperial rescript approved it, but the Grand Council disliked speaking of new policies and requested delay.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Li Duanfen memorialized to establish the institution; the throne approved, but the Grand Council, weary of talk of reform, asked that implementation be postponed.

sentences.zh: 迄戊戌，乃奉嚴旨，促擬學章，命孫家鼐爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: It was not until the wuxu year that a stern edict was received urging the drafting of school regulations, and Sun Jianai was ordered to serve as superintendent of studies.
translations.idiomatic: Not until 1898 did a stern edict order the drafting of university regulations and appoint Sun Jianai superintendent of studies.

sentences.zh: 及政變，惟大學以萌芽早得不廢。

translations.literal: When the political coup came, only the university, because it had sprouted early, was not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: After the coup of 1898, only the university survived—because it had taken root early enough to escape abolition.

sentences.zh: 許景澄繼管學，坐論義和團被誅。

translations.literal: Xu Jingcheng succeeded as superintendent of studies and was executed on account of his discussion of the Boxers.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingcheng succeeded him as superintendent but was executed for his views on the Boxers.

sentences.zh: 兩宮西幸，百熙詣行在，以人望被斯任，於是海內欣然望興學矣。

translations.literal: When the two palaces went west, Baixi went to the temporary court. Because of his public esteem he received this appointment, and then within the seas all gladly looked to the revival of learning.
translations.idiomatic: When the court fled west, Baixi went to the temporary capital. His public standing won him the post, and across the empire people looked to him with hope for a revival of learning.

sentences.zh: 百熙奏加冀州知州吳汝綸五品卿銜，總教大學。

translations.literal: Baixi memorialized to add the fifth-rank honorary title of qing to Wu Zurun, prefect of Jizhou, and appoint him general instructor of the university.
translations.idiomatic: Baixi memorialized that Wu Zurun, prefect of Jizhou, be given fifth-rank honorary rank and appointed chief instructor of the university.

sentences.zh: 汝綸辭不應，百熙具衣冠拜之，汝綸請赴日本察視學務。

translations.literal: Zurun declined and did not accept. Baixi put on full dress and cap and bowed to him. Zurun requested to go to Japan to inspect educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zurun declined the post; Baixi donned formal dress and bowed to him in person. Zurun then asked leave to travel to Japan to study its educational system.

sentences.zh: 大學教職員皆自聘，又薪金優厚，忌嫉者衆，蜚語浸聞。

translations.literal: The university's teaching staff were all personally engaged, and their salaries were moreover generous. Those who envied them were many, and slander gradually spread.
translations.idiomatic: The university hired its own faculty on generous salaries, provoking widespread envy; rumors gradually spread.

sentences.zh: 汝綸返國，未至京，卒；

translations.literal: Zurun returned to the country but died before reaching the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zurun returned to China but died before he reached Beijing.

sentences.zh: 而百熙所倚以辦學者，門人沈兆祉亦受讒搆。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Shen Zhaozhi, a disciple on whom Baixi relied to manage the school, also suffered slander and entrapment.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Shen Zhaozhi, Baixi's disciple and the man on whom he relied to run the university, also fell victim to slander.

sentences.zh: 大學既負時謗，言官奏稱本朝定制，部官大率滿、漢相維，請更設滿大臣主教事，乃增命榮慶爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: Because the university already bore the slander of the times, censors memorialized that according to this dynasty's established practice, ministry officials were generally interwoven between Manchu and Han. They requested that a Manchu minister be additionally appointed to direct affairs, and Rongqing was then additionally appointed superintendent of studies.
translations.idiomatic: The university was already under public attack when censors argued that, by dynastic custom, ministry posts were usually shared between Manchu and Han officials. They asked that a Manchu minister be added to direct affairs, and Rongqing was appointed a second superintendent of studies.

sentences.zh: 旋別設學務處，以張亨嘉爲大學總監督，百熙權益分。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward a separate Bureau of Educational Affairs was established, with Zhang Hengjia as general supervisor of the university, and Baixi's authority was further divided.
translations.idiomatic: A separate Bureau of Educational Affairs was soon created, Zhang Hengjia was made general supervisor of the university, and Baixi's authority was further divided.

sentences.zh: 始議分建七科大學，又選派諸生游學東西洋。

translations.literal: At first it was discussed to establish separately seven specialized universities, and students were also selected and sent to study in the East and West.
translations.idiomatic: Plans were drawn up to establish seven specialized universities and to send students abroad to study in Europe and America.

sentences.zh: 榮慶意不謂可，而百熙持之堅，親至站送諸生登車。

translations.literal: Rongqing's opinion was that it could not be done, but Baixi held to it firmly and personally went to the station to see the students off as they boarded the carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Rongqing opposed the plan, but Baixi held firm and went in person to the station to see the students off.

sentences.zh: 各省之派官費生自此始。

translations.literal: The dispatch of government-funded students by the provinces began from this.
translations.idiomatic: This marked the beginning of provincially funded government scholarships for study abroad.

sentences.zh: 值張之洞入覲，命改定學章，及還鎮，復命家鼐爲管學大臣。

translations.literal: When Zhang Zhidong came to audience at court, he was ordered to revise the school regulations. When he returned to his post, Jianai was again ordered to serve as superintendent of studies.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zhidong came to court he was ordered to revise the university regulations; after he returned to his post, Jianai was again appointed superintendent of studies.

sentences.zh: 凡三管學，百熙位第三矣。

translations.literal: In all there were three superintendents of studies; Baixi ranked third.
translations.idiomatic: There were three superintendents in all; Baixi was the third.

sentences.zh: 百熙擬建分科大學，以絀於貲而止，惟創醫學及譯學館、實業館，遽謝學務。

translations.literal: Baixi planned to establish specialized branch universities, but stopped because funds were short. He only founded the medical school, the translation school, and the industrial school, and then abruptly resigned from educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Baixi planned branch universities but abandoned the project for lack of funds; he founded only the medical school, the translation school, and the industrial school, then abruptly resigned from educational affairs.

sentences.zh: 賞黃馬褂、紫禁城騎馬。

translations.literal: He was rewarded with a yellow riding jacket and permission to ride a horse within the Forbidden City.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a yellow riding jacket and permission to ride within the Forbidden City.

sentences.zh: 後歷禮部、戶部、郵傳部尚書，政務、學務、編纂官制諸大臣。

translations.literal: Later he successively served as minister of the Ministries of Rites, Revenue, and Posts and Communications, and as minister of governmental affairs, educational affairs, and compilation of the official system.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in turn as minister of rites, revenue, and posts and communications, and held posts on the committees for governmental affairs, educational affairs, and official reform.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子少保，諡文達。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted junior guardian of the heir apparent, with the posthumous name Wenda.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as junior guardian of the heir apparent with the posthumous name Wenda.

sentences.zh: 唐景崇，字春卿，廣西灌陽人。

translations.literal: Tang Jingchong, style name Chunqing, was a man of Guanyang, Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jingchong, whose style was Chunqing, came from Guanyang in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 父懋功，舉人，有學行。

translations.literal: His father Maogong was a provincial graduate and possessed learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Maogong had passed the provincial examinations and was known for learning and integrity.

sentences.zh: 景崇，同治十年進士，授編修。

translations.literal: Jingchong became a jinshi in the tenth year of Tongzhi and was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong passed the jinshi examinations in the tenth year of the Tongzhi reign and was appointed a Hanlin reviser.

sentences.zh: 由侍讀四遷至內閣學士。

translations.literal: From reader-in-waiting he was transferred four times until he reached grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from reader-in-waiting through four promotions to grand secretary of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十年，典試廣東。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Guangxu he presided over the examination in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of the Guangxu reign he presided over the Guangdong provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年，主會試。

translations.literal: The next year he directed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he directed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部、禮部侍郎，權左都御史，出督浙江學政，母憂歸。

translations.literal: He successively served as vice minister of the Ministries of War and Rites, acted as left censor-in-chief, went out to supervise educational affairs in Zhejiang, and returned home on his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as vice minister of war and of rites, acted as left censor-in-chief, was sent out as Zhejiang educational commissioner, and returned home to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 拳禍起，命督辦廣西團練。

translations.literal: When the Boxer calamity arose, he was ordered to supervise and manage the militia training in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer crisis erupted he was ordered to organize militia training in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以工部侍郎典試浙江，督江蘇學政，三十一年，詔罷科歲試，學政專司考校學務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, as vice minister of the Ministry of Works he presided over the Zhejiang examination and supervised educational affairs in Jiangsu. In the thirty-first year an edict abolished the annual examination of the civil-service curriculum; educational commissioners were to specialize solely in examining and regulating educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, as vice minister of works, he presided over the Zhejiang examination and served as Jiangsu educational commissioner. In the thirty-first year an edict abolished the annual classical examination; educational commissioners were henceforth to devote themselves solely to overseeing schools.

sentences.zh: 景崇條上十事。

translations.literal: Jingchong itemized and submitted ten matters.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong submitted a ten-point program.

sentences.zh: 明年，罷學政，還京供職。

translations.literal: The next year the post of educational commissioner was abolished, and he returned to the capital to take up office.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the educational commissionership was abolished, and he returned to Beijing to resume court duties.

sentences.zh: 疏陳立憲大要四事。

translations.literal: He memorialized setting forth four main points of constitutional government.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized outlining four essentials of constitutional government.

sentences.zh: 時兩廣疆臣建議廣西省會移治南寧，京朝官皆持異議。

translations.literal: At the time the frontier officials of the two Guang provinces proposed moving the provincial capital of Guangxi to Nanning. Officials at the capital all held differing views.
translations.idiomatic: The governors-general of the two Guang provinces then proposed moving the Guangxi provincial capital to Nanning, and most capital officials disagreed.

sentences.zh: 景崇奏陳：「遷省之議，以越南逼近龍州，法人時蓄狡謀，桂林距離遠，聲氣難通，不若改建南寧之便。

translations.literal: Jingchong memorialized, stating: "The proposal to move the provincial seat holds that because Vietnam presses close upon Longzhou and the French at times harbor crafty designs, and Guilin is far in distance so that voice and influence are hard to communicate, it would be more convenient to rebuild at Nanning."
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong wrote: "Those who favor moving the capital argue that Vietnam lies close to Longzhou, that the French constantly harbor designs, and that Guilin is too remote for effective control—Nanning would be more convenient."

sentences.zh: 臣謂不然，今我兵力尚不能經營邕州，扼北海水陸衝要，徒虛張聲勢，招外人疑忌何爲？

translations.literal: Your subject says this is not so. Now our military strength still cannot manage Yongzhou, hold the land and water strategic points of the Beihai, and merely inflate reputation without substance—what is the use of provoking foreigners' suspicion and jealousy?
translations.idiomatic: "I disagree. Our forces cannot yet hold Yongzhou or the strategic land and sea approaches to Beihai; to move the capital would only inflate our reputation without substance and invite foreign suspicion—what would be gained?"

sentences.zh: 且遷徙締造之費，桂林善後之費，練兵設防之費，皆非巨款不辦。

translations.literal: Moreover, the expenses of migration and construction, the expenses of settling affairs at Guilin, and the expenses of training troops and setting defenses—all cannot be managed without huge funds.
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover, the costs of relocation and new construction, of settling affairs at Guilin, and of training troops and building defenses could not be met without enormous sums."

sentences.zh: 方今俄居西陲，英窺南徼，蒙、藏、川、滇勢均岌岌，非獨一法人之可畏。

translations.literal: At present Russia occupies the western frontier, England peers at the southern borderlands, and Mongolia, Tibet, Sichuan, and Yunnan are all in peril alike—it is not only the French who are to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: "Russia presses the western frontier, Britain watches the southern marches, and Mongolia, Tibet, Sichuan, and Yunnan are all precarious—it is not the French alone we must fear."

sentences.zh: 以大局論，決不能竭全力事廣西之一隅；

translations.literal: Speaking from the larger situation, one certainly cannot exhaust full strength on one corner of Guangxi alone.
translations.idiomatic: "From the standpoint of the empire as a whole, we cannot pour all our strength into one corner of Guangxi alone."

sentences.zh: 以廣西論，亦不能竭全力事南寧之一隅：明矣。

translations.literal: Speaking from Guangxi, one also cannot exhaust full strength on one corner of Nanning alone: this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: "And from Guangxi's own standpoint, the province cannot pour all its strength into Nanning alone—that much is clear."

sentences.zh: 故爲今之計，誠能簡重臣駐龍州，於對汛邊地二千里，相度土宜，興辦樹藝、屯墾、畜牧、開礦諸端，俟地利漸興，人齒漸繁，再以兵法部勒。

translations.literal: Therefore for the present plan, if one can truly select a weighty minister to station at Longzhou, and within two thousand li of the borderlands facing mutual garrison duty survey the suitability of the soil and undertake tree planting, reclamation colonies, animal husbandry, and opening mines on all sides, waiting until the advantages of the land gradually flourish and population gradually grows dense, and then organize them by military law—
translations.idiomatic: "The better course is to appoint a senior official to Longzhou and, along two thousand li of the border, survey local conditions and promote forestry, land reclamation, animal husbandry, and mining. When the land grows productive and population increases, troops can then be organized there by military discipline."

sentences.zh: 此上策也。

translations.literal: this is the superior policy.
translations.idiomatic: "That is the best policy."

sentences.zh: 至目前應變之方，莫如迅設龍州電綫，移提督駐南寧，增募十營，暫停廣西應解賠款，飭各省欠解廣西協餉，分年攤解，用抵賠款。

translations.literal: As for the present method of responding to change, nothing is better than swiftly establishing a telegraph line at Longzhou, moving the provincial military commander to station at Nanning, increasing recruitment by ten battalions, temporarily suspending Guangxi's payable indemnity contributions, and ordering the provinces' arrears in cooperative pay owed to Guangxi to be apportioned and paid over years to offset the indemnity.
translations.idiomatic: "For immediate measures, we should quickly install a telegraph line at Longzhou, move the provincial military commander to Nanning, recruit ten additional battalions, suspend Guangxi's indemnity payments for the time being, and order the provinces to pay their arrears of cooperative funds to Guangxi in annual installments to cover the indemnity."

sentences.zh: 一轉移間，餉足則兵强，可紓朝廷南顧之憂。

translations.literal: In one shift, if pay is sufficient then troops are strong, and the court's anxious looking to the south can be relieved.
translations.idiomatic: "With these changes, adequate pay would strengthen the troops and ease the court's anxiety over the south."

sentences.zh: 若遷省之舉，勞民費財，無益於治。

translations.literal: As for the move of the provincial seat, it burdens the people and wastes wealth, with no benefit to governance.
translations.idiomatic: "Moving the provincial capital, by contrast, would burden the people, waste money, and do nothing for good government."

sentences.zh: 」事得寢。

translations.literal: The matter was thereby laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was dropped.

sentences.zh: 調吏部侍郎，充經筵講官。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel and served as lecturer at the classics mat lectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of personnel and appointed lecturer at the classics mat.

sentences.zh: 景崇以績學端品受主知，屢司文柄。

translations.literal: Jingchong, because of his solid learning and upright character, received the ruler's trust and repeatedly held the literary brush of authority.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong won the throne's trust through solid scholarship and upright character, and he repeatedly held authority over the examinations.

sentences.zh: 迨科舉罷，廷試游學畢業生，皆倚景崇校閱。

translations.literal: When the civil-service examinations were abolished, the palace examination of students graduating from study abroad all relied on Jingchong for examination and review.
translations.idiomatic: After the civil examinations were abolished, the palace examination of students returning from study abroad was entrusted to Jingchong for review.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，戴鴻慈卒，遺疏薦景崇堪大用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong, Dai Hongci died. In his final memorial he recommended that Jingchong was fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuantong reign Dai Hongci died; in his final memorial he recommended Jingchong as fit for high office.

sentences.zh: 二年，擢學部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to minister of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was promoted to minister of education.

sentences.zh: 明年，詔設內閣，改學務大臣。

translations.literal: The next year an edict established the cabinet, and he was changed to minister of educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, when the cabinet was created by edict, he was made minister of educational affairs.

sentences.zh: 是時學說紛歧，景崇力謀溝通新舊，慎擇教科書。

translations.literal: At that time doctrines were divided and conflicting. Jingchong strove to bridge old and new and carefully selected textbooks.
translations.idiomatic: Doctrines were then sharply divided; Jingchong worked to reconcile old and new learning and chose textbooks with care.

sentences.zh: 兼任弼德院顧問大臣。

translations.literal: He concurrently served as advisory minister of the Bide Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as advisory minister of the Bide Academy.

sentences.zh: 武昌變起，袁世凱總理內閣，仍命掌學務。

translations.literal: When the Wuchang uprising arose, Yuan Shikai became premier of the cabinet and still ordered him to manage educational affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuchang uprising broke out, Yuan Shikai headed the cabinet but still left him in charge of educational affairs.

sentences.zh: 引疾去。

translations.literal: He pleaded illness and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 越三年，卒，諡文簡。

translations.literal: Three years later he died and was given the posthumous name Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died and was given the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 景崇博覽羣書，通天文算術，尤喜治史。

translations.literal: Jingchong read widely among all books, was versed in astronomy and mathematics, and especially delighted in studying history.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong read widely, was versed in astronomy and mathematics, and especially loved historical study.

sentences.zh: 自爲編修時，取新唐書爲作注，大例有三：曰糾繆，曰補闕，曰疏解，甄采書逾數百種。

translations.literal: From the time he was a reviser he took the New Book of Tang and wrote commentary on it. The great categories were three: correcting errors, filling omissions, and explaining and resolving. Books selected and gathered exceeded several hundred kinds.
translations.idiomatic: As early as his days as a Hanlin reviser he undertook a commentary on the New Book of Tang under three headings: correcting errors, filling gaps, and clarifying difficult passages, drawing on more than several hundred works.

sentences.zh: 家故貧，得秘籍精本，輒典質購之。

translations.literal: His family had long been poor. Whenever he obtained rare books and fine editions, he would pawn items to purchase them.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor; whenever he found a rare or fine edition he would pawn belongings to buy it.

sentences.zh: 殫精畢世，唯缺地理志內羈縻州及藝文志，餘均脫稿。

translations.literal: He exhausted his spirit through his lifetime. Only the Jimi prefectures within the Treatise on Geography and the Treatise on Literature were lacking; the rest were all completed in draft.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted his life to the work; only the sections on Jimi prefectures in the Treatise on Geography and the Treatise on Literature remained unfinished, while the rest existed in completed draft.

sentences.zh: 于式枚，字晦若，賀縣人。

translations.literal: Yu Shimei, style name Huiruo, was a man of Hexian.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shimei, whose style was Huiruo, came from Hexian.

sentences.zh: 博聞强記，善屬文。

translations.literal: He was broadly informed with a powerful memory and skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely learned, possessed a remarkable memory, and wrote with skill.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年進士，以庶吉士，散館用兵部主事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu he became a jinshi. As a bachelor of the Hanlin Academy, upon leaving the academy he was assigned as a secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examinations in the sixth year of the Guangxu reign, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and on leaving the academy was assigned as a secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章疏調北洋差遣，歷十餘年，奏牘多出其手。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang memorialized to transfer him to service on the Northern Sea mission. Over more than ten years, many memorials and documents came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang had him transferred to the Beiyang administration, where for more than ten years many of the region's memorials and documents came from his pen.

sentences.zh: 性不樂爲外吏，又格於例不得保升京秩，久之不遷。

translations.literal: By nature he did not delight in serving as an outside official, and moreover he was blocked by precedent from being recommended for promotion to capital rank, so for a long time he was not transferred.
translations.idiomatic: He disliked service outside the capital, and precedent barred him from promotion to Beijing rank, so for years he received no advancement.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，鴻章賀俄皇加冕，因歷聘德、法、英、美諸國，式枚充隨員。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year Hongzhang went to congratulate the Russian emperor on his coronation and thereby made successive embassies to Germany, France, England, America, and other states. Shimei served as an attendant member.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year Hongzhang traveled to congratulate the Russian emperor on his coronation and then toured Germany, France, Britain, and the United States; Shimei accompanied the mission.

sentences.zh: 俄選授禮部主事，由員外郎授御史，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he was selected and appointed secretary in the Ministry of Rites. From vice director he was appointed censor and was transferred to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Rites, then made a censor from the rank of vice director, and later promoted to supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 贊辛丑和約，賞五品京堂。

translations.literal: He assisted in the Xinchou peace treaty and was rewarded with fifth-rank capital bureau rank.
translations.idiomatic: For his work on the Boxer Protocol he was rewarded with fifth-rank capital bureau rank.

sentences.zh: 充政務處幫提調、大學堂總辦、譯學館監督。

translations.literal: He served as assistant coordinator of the Bureau of Governmental Affairs, general manager of the university, and supervisor of the translation school.
translations.idiomatic: He served as assistant coordinator of the Bureau of Governmental Affairs, general manager of the Imperial University, and supervisor of the translation school.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，以鴻臚寺少卿督廣東學政，改提學使，疏辭，命總理廣西鐵路。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, as vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments he supervised educational affairs in Guangdong and was changed to educational commissioner. He memorialized to decline, and was ordered to take overall charge of the Guangxi railway.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year he was sent as Guangdong educational commissioner with the rank of vice director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then named educational commissioner; he declined by memorial and was ordered instead to direct the Guangxi railway.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，擢郵傳部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Posts and Communications.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was promoted to vice minister of posts and communications.

sentences.zh: 當是時，政潮激烈，有詔預備立憲，舉朝競言西法，無敢持異議者。

translations.literal: At that time the political tide was fierce. An edict ordered preparation for constitutional government. The whole court vied in speaking of Western methods, and none dared hold differing views.
translations.idiomatic: Political passions were running high. An edict called for preparation toward constitutional government, and the whole court competed in praise of Western models; few dared dissent.

sentences.zh: 於是式枚奉命出使德國，充考察憲政大臣。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shimei received orders to go on mission to Germany as minister investigating constitutional government.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei was then ordered to Germany as minister charged with investigating constitutional government.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，疏言：「憲政必以本國爲根據，采取他國以輔益之，在求其實，不徒震其名。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure he memorialized, saying: "Constitutional government must take one's own country as the foundation and adopt other countries to supplement and enrich it. The aim lies in seeking what is real, not merely being awed by the name."
translations.idiomatic: Before his departure he wrote: "Constitutional government must rest on one's own country as its foundation and borrow from others only to supplement it. The aim is substance, not awe at a name."

sentences.zh: 我朝道監百王，科條詳備，行政皆守部章，風聞亦許言事，刑賞予奪，曾不自私。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's Way oversees the hundred kings. Statutes and regulations are detailed and complete. Administration all observes ministry regulations. Rumors are also permitted to be reported as matters. Punishment, reward, granting, and taking have never been selfish.
translations.idiomatic: "Our dynasty's Way has overseen a hundred generations of kings. Its statutes are detailed; administration follows ministry regulations; rumors may be reported upward; rewards and punishments have never been arbitrary."

sentences.zh: 有大政事、大興革，內則集廷臣之議，外或待疆吏之章。

translations.literal: For great political affairs and great innovations and abolitions, within the court the opinions of court ministers are gathered; outside, one sometimes waits for memorials from frontier officials.
translations.idiomatic: "On great policies and great reforms the court gathers its ministers' counsel; in the provinces it awaits the frontier officials' memorials."

sentences.zh: 勤求民隱，博采公論，與立憲之制無不符合。

translations.literal: Diligently seeking the people's hidden grievances and broadly gathering public opinion in no way fail to accord with the constitutional system.
translations.idiomatic: "In diligently seeking the people's grievances and broadly gathering public opinion, it already accords with constitutional practice."

sentences.zh: 上有教誡無約誓，下有遵守無要求。

translations.literal: Above there is instruction and admonition without covenant and oath; below there is observance without demand.
translations.idiomatic: "Above, the ruler instructs without binding oaths; below, subjects obey without making demands."

sentences.zh: 至日久官吏失職，或有奉行之不善，海國開通，又有事例之所無，自可因時損益，並非變法更張。

translations.literal: As for officials over time losing their posts, or there being poor execution of what is upheld, and maritime countries being opened, with matters for which there are no precedents, one may naturally increase or decrease according to the times—this is not reforming the law and changing policy.
translations.idiomatic: "When officials fail in their duties, when policies are poorly executed, or when maritime contact creates situations without precedent, adjustments may be made in due course—this is not a wholesale change of law."

sentences.zh: 惟人心趣向各異，告以堯、舜、周、孔之道，則以爲不足法；

translations.literal: Only people's inclinations and directions differ. Tell them the Way of Yao, Shun, the Zhou, and Confucius, and they think it insufficient as a model.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet minds differ. Tell them of the Way of Yao, Shun, the Zhou, and Confucius, and they deem it insufficient as a model."

sentences.zh: 告以英、德、法、美之制度，而日本所模仿者，則心悅誠服，以爲當行。

translations.literal: Tell them the systems of England, Germany, France, and America—and what Japan imitated—and they are pleased in heart and sincere in submission, holding that it should be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: "Tell them of the systems of Britain, Germany, France, and America—and of what Japan imitated—and they submit wholeheartedly, believing these should be adopted at once."

sentences.zh: 考日本維新之初，即宣言立憲之意。

translations.literal: Examining the beginning of Japan's restoration, it at once proclaimed the intention of establishing a constitution.
translations.idiomatic: "Japan at the outset of its restoration proclaimed its intention to establish a constitution."

sentences.zh: 後十四年，始發布開設國會之敕諭，二十年乃頒行憲法。

translations.literal: Fourteen years later it first issued an imperial rescript on opening a national assembly; only after twenty years did it promulgate the constitution.
translations.idiomatic: "Fourteen years passed before it issued an edict on opening a national assembly; only after twenty years did it promulgate a constitution."

sentences.zh: 蓋預備詳密遲慎如此。

translations.literal: Thus its preparation was detailed, slow, and cautious to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: "Its preparation was thus detailed, slow, and cautious."

sentences.zh: 今橫議者自謂國民，聚衆者輒云團體，數年之中，內治外交，用人行政，皆有干預之想。

translations.literal: Now those who speak rashly call themselves nationals; those who gather crowds readily speak of organizations. Within a few years, in internal governance, foreign relations, employment of men, and administration, all have thoughts of intervention.
translations.idiomatic: "Today rash critics call themselves 'the people'; crowds gather under the name of 'organizations.' Within a few years they have sought to intervene in domestic policy, foreign affairs, appointments, and administration alike."

sentences.zh: 動以立憲爲詞，紛馳電函，上厪宸慮。

translations.literal: They constantly take constitutional government as their slogan, sending telegrams in confusion, troubling the imperial mind above.
translations.idiomatic: "They invoke constitutional government at every turn, bombard the throne with telegrams, and trouble the sovereign's peace of mind."

sentences.zh: 蓋以立憲爲新奇可喜，不知吾國所自有。

translations.literal: This is because they regard constitutional government as novel and delightful, not knowing that our country already possesses it.
translations.idiomatic: "They treat constitutional government as a novelty, not knowing that our country already possesses its substance."

sentences.zh: 其關於學術者，固貽譏荒陋，以立憲爲即可施行，不審東洋之近事。

translations.literal: As for what concerns learning, it indeed invites ridicule for crudeness, holding that constitutional government can be implemented at once without examining recent events in the Eastern Ocean.
translations.idiomatic: "In scholarship they invite ridicule for crudeness; in politics they assume a constitution can be enacted immediately, without studying recent events in Japan."

sentences.zh: 關於政術者，尤有害治安。

translations.literal: As for what concerns political method, it is especially harmful to public order.
translations.idiomatic: "In statecraft it is especially dangerous to public order."

sentences.zh: 惟在朝廷本一定之指歸，齊萬衆之心志，循序漸進。

translations.literal: It lies only in the court taking a fixed direction as its foundation, aligning the hearts and minds of the myriad people, and advancing step by step in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: "The court must hold to a fixed course, align the people's minds, and advance step by step."

sentences.zh: 先設京師議院以定從違，舉辦地方自治以植根本，尤要在廣興教育，儲備人才。

translations.literal: First establish a capital assembly to determine assent and dissent, undertake local self-government to plant the root foundation, and above all expand education widely and store up talent.
translations.idiomatic: "It should first establish a capital assembly to register assent and dissent, promote local self-government to lay foundations, and above all expand education and train talent."

sentences.zh: 凡與憲政相輔而行者，均當先事綢繆者也。

translations.literal: All matters that assist constitutional government in proceeding together should be planned beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: "All measures that must accompany constitutional government should be prepared in advance."

sentences.zh: 臣前隨李鴻章至柏林，略觀大概。

translations.literal: Your subject formerly followed Li Hongzhang to Berlin and observed the general outline.
translations.idiomatic: "Your subject once accompanied Li Hongzhang to Berlin and observed its general arrangements."

sentences.zh: 今承特簡，謹當參合中、西同異，歸極於皇朝典章，庶言皆有本而事屬可行。

translations.literal: Now receiving special selection, I respectfully shall combine Chinese and Western similarities and differences and return to the ultimate in the imperial court's statutes, so that words all have foundation and affairs belong to what can be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: "Now specially appointed to this mission, I shall compare Chinese and Western practice and ground my report in the dynasty's own institutions, so that my words have foundation and my proposals may be carried out."

sentences.zh: 是臣區區之至願。

translations.literal: This is your subject's humble utmost wish.
translations.idiomatic: "That is this humble servant's earnest wish."

sentences.zh: 明年，調禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 時新黨要求實行立憲，召集國會日亟。

translations.literal: At the time the new faction demanded the implementation of constitutional government, and the day for convening a national assembly grew urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The reform party then pressed for immediate constitutional government and an urgent convening of a national assembly.

sentences.zh: 式枚上言：「臣徧考東西歷史，參校同異，大抵中法皆定自上而下奉行，西法則定自下而上遵守。

translations.literal: Shimei submitted, saying: "Your subject has broadly examined Eastern and Western history and compared similarities and differences. Generally, Chinese methods are all fixed from above downward for implementation, while Western methods are fixed from below upward for observance."
translations.idiomatic: Shimei wrote: "Having examined Eastern and Western history, I find that Chinese methods are generally imposed from above downward, whereas Western methods are established from below upward."

sentences.zh: 惟日本憲法，則纂自日臣伊藤博文，雖西國之名詞，仍東洋之性質。

translations.literal: Only Japan's constitution was compiled by the Japanese minister Ito Hirobumi. Although it uses Western terms, it still has an Eastern Ocean character.
translations.idiomatic: "Japan's constitution alone was drafted by Ito Hirobumi: though it uses Western terms, it retains an East Asian character."

sentences.zh: 其采取則普魯士爲多，其本原則德君臣所定，名爲欽定憲法。

translations.literal: What it adopted was mostly Prussia; its origin was fixed by the ruler and ministers of Germany, and it is called an imperially granted constitution.
translations.idiomatic: "It drew chiefly on Prussia; its foundation was laid by the German sovereign and his ministers, and it is called an imperially granted constitution."

sentences.zh: 夫國所以立曰政，政所以行曰權，權所歸即利所在。

translations.literal: A state is established through what is called government; government is carried out through what is called power; where power resides is where benefit lies.
translations.idiomatic: "A state stands through government; government operates through power; where power rests is where advantage lies."

sentences.zh: 定於一則無非分之想，散於衆則有競進之心。

translations.literal: When fixed in one there are no thoughts of overstepping one's portion; when scattered among the multitude there is a mind of competing advance.
translations.idiomatic: "When power is fixed in one place, men do not entertain extravagant ambitions; when it is dispersed among many, rivalry arises."

sentences.zh: 行之而善，則爲日本之維新；

translations.literal: If carried out well, it becomes Japan's restoration.
translations.idiomatic: "If well executed, the result is Japan's restoration."

sentences.zh: 行之不善，則爲法國之革命。

translations.literal: If carried out poorly, it becomes France's revolution.
translations.idiomatic: "If poorly executed, the result is France's revolution."

sentences.zh: 法國當屢世苛虐之後，民困已深，欲以立憲救亡，而適促其亂。

translations.literal: France, after generations of harsh cruelty, had the people's distress already deep. Wishing to save the state through establishing a constitution, it instead hastened its disorder.
translations.idiomatic: "France, after generations of harsh rule, was deeply exhausted; seeking salvation through a constitution, it only hastened disorder."

sentences.zh: 日本當尊王傾幕之時，本由民力，故以立憲爲報，而猶緩其期。

translations.literal: Japan, at the time of honoring the sovereign and overthrowing the shogunate, originally relied on the people's strength, and therefore took establishing a constitution as repayment, yet still delayed the term.
translations.idiomatic: "Japan, in the movement to restore the emperor and overthrow the shogunate, owed its success to popular effort and therefore offered a constitution in return—yet even so delayed the timetable."

sentences.zh: 中國名義最重，政治最寬，國體尊嚴，人情安習，既無法國之怨毒，又非日本之改造。

translations.literal: China places greatest weight on names and principles, and its politics are most lenient. The dignity of the state structure and popular habits of peaceful custom—there is neither France's bitter resentment nor Japan's transformation.
translations.idiomatic: "China places the greatest weight on legitimacy; its politics are lenient; its state dignity and popular habits are settled. It has neither France's bitter resentment nor Japan's revolutionary transformation."

sentences.zh: 皇上俯順輿情，迭降諭旨，分定年期，自宜互相奮勉，靜待推行。

translations.literal: The emperor bows to follow public sentiment, repeatedly issuing edicts and fixing the term of years. Naturally all should encourage one another and quietly await implementation.
translations.idiomatic: "The emperor has bowed to public sentiment, issued repeated edicts, and fixed a timetable; all should encourage one another and await implementation in patience."

sentences.zh: 豈容欲速等於取償，求治同於論價？

translations.literal: How can one allow haste to equal demanding repayment, or seeking good government to equal haggling over price?
translations.idiomatic: "How can impatience be tolerated, as if demanding immediate payment, or governance be bargained over like a price?"

sentences.zh: 至敢言監督朝廷，推倒政府，胥動浮言，幾同亂黨。

translations.literal: As for daring to speak of supervising the court, overthrowing the government—all move with empty words and are nearly like disorderly factions.
translations.idiomatic: "As for those who dare speak of supervising the throne and overthrowing the government—all trade in empty talk and are nearly indistinguishable from rebels."

sentences.zh: 欲圖補救之策，惟在朝廷舉錯一秉至公，不稍予以指摘之端，自無從爲煽惑之計。

translations.literal: If one wishes to plan remedial measures, it lies only in the court's actions and errors all holding to utmost fairness, not giving the slightest opening for criticism, so that there is naturally no means for schemes of incitement.
translations.idiomatic: "The remedy lies in the court holding strictly to fairness and giving no opening for attack, so that agitators find no foothold."

sentences.zh: 至東南各省疆吏，當慎擇有風力、知大體者鎮懾之。

translations.literal: As for the frontier officials of the southeastern provinces, one should carefully choose those with force of character who understand the larger principles to suppress and awe them.
translations.idiomatic: "In the southeast, frontier officials of force and sound judgment should be chosen to keep order."

sentences.zh: 當十年預備之期，爲大局安危所繫。

translations.literal: The ten-year preparatory period bears on the safety or peril of the larger situation.
translations.idiomatic: "The ten-year preparatory period bears on the safety of the whole realm."

sentences.zh: 日皇所謂『組織權限，爲朕親裁』，德相所謂『法定於君，非民可解』。

translations.literal: What the Japanese emperor called "organizing authority is personally adjudicated by Us," and what the German chancellor called "law is fixed by the sovereign and is not for the people to interpret."
translations.idiomatic: "As the Japanese emperor said, 'The organization of authority is personally adjudicated by Us'; as the German chancellor said, 'Law is fixed by the sovereign and is not for the people to interpret.'"

sentences.zh: 故必正名定分，然後措正施行。

translations.literal: Therefore one must rectify names and fix distinctions, and only then can measures be rightly implemented.
translations.idiomatic: "Names and ranks must first be fixed; only then can policy be rightly carried out."

sentences.zh: 臣濫膺考察，斷不敢附會時趨，貽誤國家，得罪名教。

translations.literal: Your subject has undeservedly received this investigation commission and absolutely dares not echo the current trend, bring error to the state, or offend the teachings of names and principles.
translations.idiomatic: "Your unworthy servant, entrusted with this investigation, dares not echo the fashion of the day, harm the state, or offend the teachings of the sages."

sentences.zh: 」章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the responsible office.

sentences.zh: 尋調吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 上海政聞社法部主事陳景仁等電請定三年內開國會，罷式枚謝天下，嚴旨申飭，褫景仁職。

translations.literal: Chen Jingren of the Ministry of Justice in Shanghai's Political News Society and others telegraphed requesting that a national assembly be fixed to open within three years and that Shimei be dismissed to apologize to the realm. A stern edict rebuked them and stripped Jingren of office.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingren and others of Shanghai's Political News Society telegraphed demanding a national assembly within three years and Shimei's dismissal. A stern edict rebuked them and stripped Jingren of his office.

sentences.zh: 式枚復奏言：「德皇接受國書，答言憲政紛繁，慮未必合中國用，選舉法尤未易行。

translations.literal: Shimei again memorialized, saying: "When the German emperor received the credentials, he replied that constitutional government is intricate and complex, and he feared it might not suit China's use; election law is especially not easy to implement."
translations.idiomatic: Shimei memorialized again: "When the German emperor received our credentials, he replied that constitutional government is intricate and may not suit China; election law would be especially difficult to implement."

sentences.zh: 又昔英儒斯賓塞爾亦甚言憲法流弊，謂美國憲法本人民平等，行之久而治權握於政黨，平民不勝其苦。

translations.literal: Moreover, the former English scholar Spencer also spoke at length of the abuses of constitutional government, saying that the American constitution was originally based on equality of the people, but after long implementation governing power was held by political parties and common people could not bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: "The English scholar Spencer also warned of constitutional abuses, noting that though the American constitution was founded on popular equality, in time governing power fell to political parties and the common people suffered."

sentences.zh: 蓋歐人言憲法，其難其慎如此。

translations.literal: Thus when Europeans speak of constitutional government, its difficulty and caution are to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: "Such is the difficulty and caution with which Europeans regard constitutional government."

sentences.zh: 今橫議遍於國中，上則詆政府固權，下則罵國民失職，專以爭競相勸導。

translations.literal: Now rash opinion spreads throughout the country. Above they slander the government for monopolizing power; below they revile nationals for failing in duty, exclusively encouraging rivalry and competition.
translations.idiomatic: "Today rash opinion fills the land: above, the government is accused of monopolizing power; below, the people are blamed for failing their duty—all while rivalry is encouraged."

sentences.zh: 此正斯賓塞爾所云政黨者流，與平民固無與也。

translations.literal: This is precisely what Spencer called the class of political parties, which in fact has nothing to do with common people.
translations.idiomatic: "This is precisely what Spencer called the party class, which has nothing to do with the common people."

sentences.zh: 伊藤博文論君臣相與，先道德而後科條。

translations.literal: Ito Hirobumi discussed the relation between ruler and minister, putting morality first and regulations afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Ito Hirobumi held that relations between ruler and minister require morality before statutes.

sentences.zh: 君民何獨不然？

translations.literal: Why should relations between ruler and people alone not be so?
translations.idiomatic: Why should relations between ruler and people be any different?

sentences.zh: 果能誠信相接，則普與日本以欽定憲法行之至今；

translations.literal: If sincerity and trust can truly connect, then Prussia and Japan have carried out an imperially granted constitution to the present day.
translations.idiomatic: "If sincerity and trust truly prevail, then Prussia and Japan have carried an imperially granted constitution down to the present."

sentences.zh: 如其不然，則法蘭西固民約憲法，何以革命者再三，改法者數十而猶未定？

translations.literal: If not so, then France indeed has a constitution of popular covenant—why have revolutions come again and again, and changes of law numbered in the tens yet still not been settled?
translations.idiomatic: "If not, then France, for all its popular covenant constitution, has seen repeated revolutions and dozens of constitutional revisions without ever settling its affairs."

sentences.zh: 臣愚以爲中國立憲，應以日本仿照普魯士之例爲權衡，以畢士麥由君主用人民意見制定，及伊藤博文先道德後科條之言爲標準，則憲法大綱立矣。

translations.literal: Your subject foolishly holds that in China's establishing a constitution, one should take Japan's imitation of the Prussian example as the measure, and take Bismarck's formulation by the sovereign using the people's opinions, together with Ito Hirobumi's words on morality before regulations, as the standard—then the great outline of the constitution will be established.
translations.idiomatic: "I hold that China in establishing a constitution should take Japan's imitation of Prussia as its measure, Bismarck's principle that the sovereign shapes law with popular counsel, and Ito's insistence on morality before statutes as its standards—then the constitutional outline will be sound."

sentences.zh: 」章下所司。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the responsible office.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the responsible office.

sentences.zh: 又以各省諮議局章程與普國地方議會制度不符，大恉謂：「改革未定之時，中央政權唯恐少統一堅强之力，而國民識政體知法意者極少。

translations.literal: He also held that the regulations of the provincial deliberative assemblies did not accord with the Prussian local assembly system and denounced them greatly, saying: "At a time when reform is not yet settled, central political power fears only lacking unified and strong force, while nationals who understand the political system and know the meaning of law are extremely few."
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked the provincial deliberative assembly regulations as incompatible with the Prussian local assembly system, declaring: "While reform remains unsettled, central authority can scarcely afford to lose unified strength, and few citizens understand political institutions or the meaning of law."

sentences.zh: 驟以此龐大政權之地方議會，橫亙政府與國民之間，縱使被選者不皆營私武斷，而一國政權落於最少數人之手，劫持中外大臣，後患何可勝言？

translations.literal: Suddenly to place this enormous political power of local assemblies across between government and nationals—even if those elected are not all scheming for private gain and arbitrary rule—yet a state's political power falls into the hands of the smallest number of people, who can coerce Chinese and foreign ministers. What later harm can be fully described?
translations.idiomatic: "To thrust such powerful local assemblies between government and people—even if not every member is corrupt—would place national power in the hands of a tiny minority able to coerce ministers at home and abroad. The consequences are incalculable."

sentences.zh: 」因證以普制，逐條駁議。

translations.literal: He therefore verified by the Prussian system and refuted the proposals article by article.
translations.idiomatic: He cited the Prussian system and refuted the proposals article by article.

sentences.zh: 先後譯奏普魯士憲法全文、官制位號等級，暨兩議院新舊選舉法。

translations.literal: In succession he translated and memorialized the full text of the Prussian constitution, official ranks and titles and grades, together with the old and new election laws of the two chambers.
translations.idiomatic: He successively translated and submitted the full Prussian constitution, the ranks and titles of officials, and the old and new election laws of the two chambers.

sentences.zh: 式枚以三十三年冬行，宣統元年六月返國，以疾乞假。

translations.literal: Shimei departed in the winter of the thirty-third year, returned to the country in the sixth month of the first year of Xuantong, and pleaded illness to request leave.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei departed in the winter of the thirty-third year, returned in the sixth month of the first Xuantong year, and requested leave on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 張之洞遺疏薦式枚堪大用。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhidong, in his final memorial, recommended that Shimei was fit for great employment.
translations.idiomatic: In his final memorial Zhang Zhidong recommended Shimei as fit for high office.

sentences.zh: 轉吏部侍郎，改學部侍郎，總理禮學館事、修訂法律大臣、國史館副總裁。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, changed to vice minister of the Ministry of Education, and took overall charge of the Ritual Learning Academy, served as minister for revising the laws, and was vice president of the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice minister of personnel, then to vice minister of education, and directed the Ritual Learning Academy while serving as minister for legal revision and vice president of the National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 國變後，僑居青島。

translations.literal: After the change of dynasty he lived abroad in Qingdao.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he lived in exile in Qingdao.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年六十三，諡文和。

translations.literal: Before long he died, at the age of sixty-three, and was given the posthumous name Wenhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at sixty-three, and was given the posthumous name Wenhe.

sentences.zh: 式枚生而隱宮，精力絕人，夜倚枕坐如枯僧。

translations.literal: Shimei was born with a hidden palace [defect]. His energy was surpassing. At night he sat leaning on a pillow like a withered monk.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei was born with a hidden physical defect yet possessed extraordinary energy; at night he would sit upright against his pillow like an ascetic monk.

sentences.zh: 內介而外和易。

translations.literal: Inwardly upright but outwardly easy and agreeable.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly firm, outwardly mild and approachable.

sentences.zh: 論事謇諤，頗有聲公卿間云。

translations.literal: In discussing affairs he was blunt and forthright, and had considerable reputation among the high officials.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke bluntly on public affairs and enjoyed considerable standing among the high officials.

sentences.zh: 沈家本，字子惇，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: Shen Jiaben, style name Zidun, was a man of Gui'an, Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Jiaben, whose style was Zidun, came from Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少讀書，好深湛之思，於周官多創獲。

translations.literal: In youth he read books and delighted in deep and profound thought. On the Offices of Zhou he had many original gains.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved reading and deep reflection, and made many original contributions to the study of the Offices of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 初援例以郎中分刑部，博稽掌故，多所纂述。

translations.literal: At first, by purchased quota he entered as a director in the Ministry of Punishments. He broadly investigated established precedents and compiled and wrote on many matters.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered the Ministry of Punishments by purchased quota as a director, where he investigated precedents extensively and compiled many works.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，成進士，仍留部。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Guangxu he became a jinshi and still remained in the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of the Guangxu reign he passed the jinshi examinations and remained at the ministry.

sentences.zh: 補官後，充主稿，兼秋審處。

translations.literal: After filling his official post, he served as chief draftsman and concurrently in the autumn review office.
translations.idiomatic: After receiving his formal appointment he served as chief draftsman and also worked in the autumn review office.

sentences.zh: 自此遂專心法律之學，爲尚書潘祖蔭所稱賞。

translations.literal: From this he then devoted his mind to the study of law and was praised and appreciated by Minister Pan Zuyin.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he devoted himself to legal studies and won the praise of Minister Pan Zuyin.

sentences.zh: 十九年，出知天津府，治尚寬大，姦民易之，聚衆鬨於市，即擒斬四人，無敢復犯者。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he went out to serve as prefect of Tianjin. His governance was still lenient and broad. Wicked people took him lightly. A crowd made a disturbance in the market, and he immediately seized and executed four men; none dared offend again.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he was appointed prefect of Tianjin. His rule was lenient, and ruffians took advantage of it until a mob rioted in the market; he immediately seized and executed four ringleaders, and no one dared repeat the offense.

sentences.zh: 調劇保定，甘軍毀法國教堂，當路懾於外勢，償五萬金，以道署舊址建新堂，侵及府署東偏。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the difficult post of Baoding. Gansu troops destroyed a French church. Those in power were intimidated by foreign pressure, paid fifty thousand taels in compensation, and built a new church on the old site of the circuit intendant's office, encroaching on the eastern side of the prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the difficult post of Baoding, where Gansu troops had destroyed a French church. The authorities, intimidated by foreign pressure, paid fifty thousand taels in compensation and built a new church on the circuit intendant's old site, encroaching on the eastern wing of the prefectural yamen.

sentences.zh: 家本據府志力爭得直。

translations.literal: Jiaben, relying on the prefectural gazetteer, strove forcefully and won the case.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaben cited the prefectural gazetteer and fought the matter through until justice was done.

sentences.zh: 拳匪亂作，家本已擢通永道、山西按察使，未及行，兩宮西幸。

translations.literal: When the Boxer turmoil arose, Jiaben had already been promoted to circuit intendant of Tongyong and surveillance commissioner of Shanxi, but before he could take up his posts the two palaces went west.
translations.idiomatic: When the Boxer uprising broke out, Jiaben had been promoted to circuit intendant of Tongyong and surveillance commissioner of Shanxi, but before he could depart the court fled west.

sentences.zh: 聯軍入保定，教士銜前隙，誣以助拳匪，卒無左驗而解。

translations.literal: When the allied armies entered Baoding, missionaries bore a previous grudge and falsely accused him of aiding the Boxers, but in the end there was no corroborating evidence and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: When the allied armies entered Baoding, missionaries who bore an old grudge accused him of aiding the Boxers, but no evidence was found and he was released.

sentences.zh: 因馳赴行在，授光祿寺卿，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: He therefore hurried to the temporary court, was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was promoted to vice minister of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried to the temporary court, was appointed director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and was promoted to vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 自各國互市以來，內地許傳教，而中外用律輕重懸殊，民、教日齟齬。

translations.literal: Since the various states began mutual trade, the interior was permitted missionary activity, yet Chinese and foreign application of law differed greatly in severity, and common people and missionaries grew daily at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Since the treaty ports opened, missionaries were allowed in the interior, yet Chinese and foreign law differed sharply in severity, and friction between common people and missionaries grew daily.

sentences.zh: 官畏事則務抑民，民不能堪，則激而一逞，往往焚戮成巨禍。

translations.literal: Officials, fearing trouble, strove to suppress the people. When the people could not bear it, they were provoked to burst forth at once, and often burning and slaughter became great calamities.
translations.idiomatic: Officials, fearing trouble, suppressed the people; when the people could bear it no longer, they erupted in violence, and burning and slaughter often followed on a catastrophic scale.

sentences.zh: 家本以謂治今日之民，當令官吏普通法律。

translations.literal: Jiaben held that in governing the people of today, officials should be made generally familiar with the law.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaben held that to govern the people of his day, officials must be made generally familiar with the law.

sentences.zh: 然中律不變而欲收回領事審判權，終不可得。
