translations.literal: Yet if Chinese law remained unchanged while one wished to recover consular jurisdiction, in the end it could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet without reforming Chinese law, consular jurisdiction could never be recovered.

sentences.zh: 會變法議起，袁世凱奏設修訂法律館，命家本偕伍廷芳總其事；

translations.literal: When discussion of reform arose, Yuan Shikai memorialized to establish the Bureau for Revising the Laws and ordered Jiaben together with Wu Tingfang to take overall charge of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When reform was debated, Yuan Shikai memorialized to establish the Bureau for Revising the Laws and appointed Jiaben and Wu Tingfang to direct it jointly.

sentences.zh: 別設法律學堂，畢業者近千人，一時稱盛。

translations.literal: A separate law school was established; those who graduated numbered nearly a thousand, and for a time it was acclaimed as flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: A law school was also established; nearly a thousand students graduated, and for a time the program was celebrated as a great success.

sentences.zh: 補大理寺卿，旋改法部侍郎，充修訂法律大臣。

translations.literal: He filled the post of director of the Court of Review, was soon changed to vice minister of the Ministry of Law, and served as minister for revising the laws.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the Court of Review, soon transferred to vice minister of law, and served as minister for legal revision.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，兼資政院副總裁，仍日與館員商訂諸法草案，先後告成，未嘗以事繁自解。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he concurrently served as vice president of the Political Consultative Council, yet still daily discussed and fixed draft laws with the bureau staff. They were completed in succession, and he never excused himself on grounds of excessive business.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuantong reign he also served as vice president of the Political Consultative Council, yet still met daily with bureau staff to draft legislation; the codes were completed one after another, and he never pleaded excessive business as an excuse to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 其所著書，有讀律校勘記、秋讞須知、刑案匯覽、刺字集、律例偶箋、歷代刑官考、歷代刑法考、漢律摭遺、明大誥竣令考、明律目箋，他所著非刑律者又二十餘種，都二百餘卷。

translations.literal: Among his written works were Collation Notes on Reading the Code, Essentials for Autumn Review, Compendium of Criminal Cases, Collection on Tattooing, Occasional Notes on Statutes and Regulations, Investigation of Punishment Officials through the Ages, Investigation of Punishment Law through the Ages, Gathered Remains of Han Law, Investigation of the Great Admonitions and Completed Commands of the Ming, and Commentary on the Ming Code Articles. His other works not on criminal law numbered more than twenty kinds, totaling more than two hundred juan.
translations.idiomatic: His writings included Collation Notes on Reading the Code, Essentials for Autumn Review, Compendium of Criminal Cases, Collection on Tattooing, Occasional Notes on Statutes and Regulations, Investigation of Punishment Officials through the Ages, Investigation of Punishment Law through the Ages, Gathered Remains of Han Law, Investigation of the Great Admonitions and Completed Commands of the Ming, and Commentary on the Ming Code Articles, together with more than twenty works on subjects other than criminal law—more than two hundred juan in all.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 論曰：自變法議興，凡新政特設大臣領之。

translations.literal: The commentator says: From the time discussion of reform arose, every new policy was specially assigned a minister to lead it.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator observes: Once reform was debated, every new policy was placed under a specially appointed minister.

sentences.zh: 百熙管學務，家本修法律，並邀時譽。

translations.literal: Baixi managed educational affairs and Jiaben revised the laws; both won the praise of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Baixi directed educational affairs and Jiaben revised the laws; both won contemporary acclaim.

sentences.zh: 景崇之主教育，謀溝通新舊；

translations.literal: Jingchong's direction of education sought to bridge old and new.
translations.idiomatic: Jingchong, in directing education, sought to bridge old and new learning.

sentences.zh: 式枚之論憲政，務因時損益。

translations.literal: Shimei's discussion of constitutional government strove to increase or decrease according to the times.
translations.idiomatic: Shimei's writings on constitutional government sought timely adjustment rather than rigid imitation.

sentences.zh: 而大勢所趨，已莫能挽救。

translations.literal: Yet the trend of the great situation could no longer be rescued.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the tide of events could no longer be turned back.

sentences.zh: 家鼐儒厚廉謹，常以資望領新政，每參大計，獨持正不阿。

translations.literal: Jianai was Confucian, generous, honest, and cautious. He often led new policies by virtue of senior standing, participated in every great plan, and alone upheld what was right without currying favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jianai was learned, generous, honest, and cautious; he often headed new policies by virtue of senior standing, took part in every major decision, and alone held to principle without trimming his views to please.

sentences.zh: 賢哉，不愧古大臣矣！

translations.literal: How worthy! He did not disgrace the great ministers of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: How worthy a man—he did not disgrace the great ministers of old!
